_comment: The toolchain that RENDERS and VALIDATES bootstrap, staged as an instance again and to become the repository litlfred/bootstrap-tools. Owner, 2026-09-29 (bean 81tw): 'we will https://github.com/litlfred/bootstrap-tools use this for the tools that render bootstrap/ but were put in cat-harness. for now create dir bootstrap-tools/ for staging split out into repo. make sure IRIs updated' -- then, choosing scope: 'need Zod usage in bootstrap tools as part of validation in rendering pipeline. will also need SEMVER skills in bootstrap-tools'. THIS REVERSES 319n (2026-09-24, 'Validate/zod in cat-harness') for the files it holds; etg1 (2026-09-20) staged the first bootstrap-tools and 319n retired it. graph.ts, requirement.ts and model-registry.ts stay in cat-harness because cat-harness imports them and this instance needs cat-harness: moving them would be a cycle.
_visibility_comment: HOW THE REPOSITORY SEES THIS INSTANCE WITHOUT CAT-HARNESS NAMING IT. The first bootstrap-tools needed a repository-scoped duplicate of its schemas/ entry in cat-harness/cat-harness.json, because resolution walks one declaration plus its DEPENDENCIES and this instance can never be a dependency of cat-harness -- it depends ON cat-harness. That duplicate would make the lower instance name the higher one, which is the arrow check:reference-direction and the owner's 2026-09-23 rule forbid. So there is no entry in cat-harness.json. What finds this instance instead is DISCOVERY: instanceRootsIn() scans the repository root one level deep for a <name>.json, so every gate that asks 'which instances are there' (check:instance-config, check:declared-assets, check:reference-direction, check:undeclared-files, instance-render) reaches this declaration as it stands. Its schema nodes are minted in ITS OWN graph document, <base>/bootstrap-tools/bootstrap-tools.jsonld#schema/<module>, by kg-export --instance ./bootstrap-tools, rather than in cat-harness's.

directories.description: The authoritative Zod for two of bootstrap's published documents -- the discussion input and output -- and for the bootstrap graph document. Generated into bootstrap/schemas/*.schema.json by `bootstrap:schemas`, with the `$id`s unchanged because they are a published contract.

The render pipeline's executable surface: the schema generator and its drawn page, the document validator, the semver calculator, the local graph builder and the outside-concept check. ENTRY POINTS, named by path in package.json and in the CI workflows.

The skills this instance owns. ONE today -- `bootstrap-contract-semver`, what MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH mean for bootstrap's published schemas and graph, and why the bump is computed from a diff rather than asserted.
